subject: Mutual action plan: unit-economics sanity check + evaluation timeline
messages:
From: Lauren Simms <lauren@acmeanalytics.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@acmeanalytics.com
Date: 2026-03-01T09:12:00-08:00
Subject: Mutual action plan — unit-econ checks before eval

Hi Marissa,

Thanks for the demo last week. We want to make sure the MAP includes a realistic cost model before we start the evaluation. Two asks from our side: 1) can you translate the MAP into explicit tokens/$ assumptions (per-request tokens, pricing basis, and expected effective tokens after caching), and 2) include the batching and throughput assumptions you used so we can validate expected monthly spend?

What would be most helpful is a short table with: avg tokens per call (prompt + response), token price (hosted vs. dedicated), KV/prefix cache hit rate assumed, batching multiplier (throughput lift) and an example 1M-call cost. We plan to run a 10k-sample eval and then scale to production if results look good.

Timeline constraints from procurement: we need a draft MAP and cost model this week (by Mar 5) to start legal/PO prep. Can you also include who at Redwood will be the primary contact for procurement questions?

Thanks,
Lauren
Director, ML Product
Acme Analytics
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Lauren Simms <lauren@acmeanalytics.com>
Cc: rishi_malhotra@redwood.com, vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com, avery_johnson@redwood.com
Date: 2026-03-02T11:30:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Mutual action plan — unit-econ checks before eval

Hi Lauren —

Appreciate the clear ask. Attached are two artifacts: acme_map_v0.9.pdf (MAP with milestones) and acme_cost_model_v1.xlsx (workbook with line-item calculations). Highlights below — I kept the numbers conservative so procurement has room for negotiation.

Summary assumptions (hosted baseline):
- Avg tokens per call (prompt + response): 550 tokens (median 420, tail up to 2k)
- Nominal token price (hosted): $0.00030 per token (equivalent to $0.30 per 1k tokens)
- KV/prefix cache hit rate: 60% (saves generated tokens on cached prefixes)
- Effective batching multiplier: avg batch size 4 -> ~2.5x throughput lift in GPU utilization

Example math (hosted):
- Raw cost per call = 550 * $0.00030 = $0.165
- With 60% cache hit saving 220 generated tokens on average -> effective tokens per call = 330 -> cost = 330 * $0.00030 = $0.099 (approx 40% savings)
- 1M raw calls (no cache) = $165,000; with 60% cache hit -> ~ $99,000

Notes on batching / throughput:
- Batching reduces per-request compute overhead and amortizes KV cache reads; we estimate 2.0–2.8x token throughput improvement depending on sequence-length variance.
- For latency-sensitive evals we can run single-request (no batching) for p95 measurements, then re-run with batching knobs for cost projections.

Next steps we propose in the MAP (dates tentative):
- Mar 9: Acme delivers 10k-sample eval prompts (anonymized)
- Mar 10–13: Redwood runs eval + cost sweep (varying cache hit and batch sizes)
- Mar 16: Joint review of results and cost sign-off
- Mar 23: Target PO date (procurement)
- Apr 6: Go-live (if PO + provisioning complete)

Primary procurement contact at Redwood: Avery Johnson (avery_johnson@redwood.com) — handles SOW/PO coordination. Rishi will own the technical cost model and run the evals.

I attached the workbook with a sample 1M-call pivot and an interactive tab where you can toggle cache hit rate and batch size. Tell us which scenarios you want prioritized and we’ll run them for the eval.

Cheers,
Marissa
Sr. Account Executive | Redwood Inference
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
To: Lauren Simms <lauren@acmeanalytics.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Cc: vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com, avery_johnson@redwood.com
Date: 2026-03-03T09:45:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Mutual action plan — unit-econ checks before eval

Lauren/Marissa — quick technical note and an alternate cost view (Dedicated pricing):

Refined assumptions (split by deployment):
1) Hosted (on-demand): $0.00030 / token (no commit) — good for short evals
2) Dedicated (reserved): equivalent effective token price ~ $0.00022 / token (volume/commit discount baked in for 6–12mo commit)

Per-call numbers:
- Avg tokens = 550 -> hosted = $0.165 / call; dedicated = $0.121 / call
- Cache impact (60% hit -> 220 tokens saved): hosted effective = $0.099 / call; dedicated effective = $0.073 / call
- If batching increases throughput 2.5x, effective per-call compute cost reduces by ~1/2.5 on amortized GPU hours; combine that with cache and you get to ~ $0.03–0.04 per call on Dedicated in our modeled workloads. (See workbook tab "combined_scenarios" for spreadsheet formulas.)

Operational assumptions to validate:
- Cache hit rate is highly sensitive to prompt template variability. If Acme side templates change >20% per request, expect hit rate to drop to ~30–35%; please confirm stability of prefix content.
- Batch size depends on latency SLO. For a p95 < 300ms target, we recommend benchmarking single-request latency first; batching gains are more valuable for throughput/steady-state cost reduction than for meeting tight p95s.

Suggested eval plan (technical):
- Deliver 10k prompts by Mar 9 (anonymized + categorized by template)
- Redwood runs: (a) baseline single-request latency and cost; (b) cache-enabled run; (c) batched run (batch sizes 2,4,8)
- We'll produce: tokens-per-call histogram, p50/p95 latency, cache-hit breakdown by template, and a 1M-call extrapolated cost table under each scenario.

I also attached redwood_map_comments.docx with inline comments on milestone acceptance criteria.

Rishi
Principal Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Lauren Simms <lauren@acmeanalytics.com>
Cc: rishi_malhotra@redwood.com, avery_johnson@redwood.com, vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com
Date: 2026-03-04T15:10:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Mutual action plan — unit-econ checks before eval

Lauren —

Thanks for the quick turnaround. I updated the MAP to include explicit acceptance criteria for the eval and a short section called "Unit-econ checkpoints" (see attached updated MAP). Key line items included in the MAP:
- Eval acceptance: p95 latency <= 300ms (single-request) AND end-to-end quality threshold (exact F1 TBD by template)
- Cost sign-off: scenario table where Acme chooses target cache hit rate and batch profile and signs off on projected monthly cost (1M-call bucket)
- Procurement items: SOW template, expected lead time for Dedicated capacity (3 weeks after PO), and standard security checklist (SOC2 reports)

If Acme confirms the following today, we can keep the timeline:
1) Deliver 10k eval prompts by Mon Mar 9
2) Confirm whether you want us to model Hosted-only or include Dedicated 6-month commit scenarios (we recommend modeling both)
3) Procurement contact to confirm PO timeline (procurement@acmeanalytics.com)

I also noted a small risk: if average tokens per call end up >800 we will need to revisit the Dedicated sizing and likely recommend a different instance family — that will change the per-token equivalent. We flagged that in the workbook.

Avery will lead procurement coordination and Vivek is looped for escalation if we need faster provisioning.

Best,
Marissa
From: Lauren Simms <lauren@acmeanalytics.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@acmeanalytics.com
Date: 2026-03-05T16:22:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Mutual action plan — unit-econ checks before eval

Marissa/Rishi —

This looks good and very thorough — appreciate the worked examples. Procurement confirms they will aim to have the PO ready by Mar 23 and we will deliver the 10k anonymized prompts by Mar 9. Please prioritize the following scenarios for the eval:
- Hosted baseline
- Dedicated 6-month commit with 60% cache hit and batch size = 4

We will review the MAP with our legal team next week and send any comments. Thanks for assigning Avery as the procurement owner — I will loop him in separately.

Thanks,
Lauren
